sentences.text: Pinpanetta is an extinct genus of birds belonging to the duck family.
The genus includes three species: P. tedfordi, P. vickersrichae, and P. fromensis.
It belongs to the subfamily Erismaturinae.
The genus was described by Worthy in 2009.
The name comes from Lake Pinpa in the Lake Eyre Basin of north-eastern South Australia.
Much of the descriptive fossil material comes from the Pinpa Local Fauna.
This bird lived in central Australia during the Late Oligocene.
Its existence spans the Chattian stage, between 27.3 and 23.04 million years ago.
